series_behind_the_chart.chart: Office of Financial Research, Short-term Funding Monitor, market digest 'Primary dealer reverse repo and securities borrowing by tenor' (chart 22): https://www.financialresearch.gov/short-term-funding-monitor/market-digests/tenor/chart-22/
series_behind_the_chart.chart_mnemonics: NYPD-PD_RRP_T_OO-A, NYPD-PD_RRP_T_L30-A, NYPD-PD_RRP_T_GE30-A, NYPD-PD_SB_T_OO-A, NYPD-PD_SB_T_L30-A, NYPD-PD_SB_T_GE30-A (read from the page's own markup on 28 October 2026): reverse repurchase agreements and securities borrowed on Treasury collateral, by tenor (overnight and open, under 30 days, 30 days or more)
series_behind_the_chart.what_the_ofr_serves: the OFR is a re-publisher of the New York Fed's FR 2004 weekly statistics (its metadata: 'Federal Reserve Bank of New York Primary Dealer Statistics', observation frequency weekly, start 2015-01-07, last update 2026-10-23 13:30:01 on the query of 28 October 2026). Its data API serves the reverse-repo mnemonics (NYPD-PD_RRP_T_*, NYPD-PD_RRP_T_TOT-A) only to 2021-12-29 and the securities-borrowed ones to 2026-10-14, so the OFR route cannot supply the reverse-repo leg for the 2026 days. The New York Fed's own API serves both legs to the current week, and is the primary source the OFR draws on.
series_behind_the_chart.chosen: the New York Fed's four Treasury totals, which are the tenor-free sums of the chart's Treasury rows, in the form the New York Fed publishes them: reverse repurchase agreements on U.S. Treasury securities excluding TIPS (PDSIRRA-UTSETTOT) and on TIPS (PDSIRRA-UTSTTOT), and securities borrowed on the same two classes (PDSIOSB-UTSETTOT, PDSIOSB-UTSTTOT). Compared on 28 October 2026 with the OFR's own totals, week by week where neither side is withheld: the sum of the two reverse-repo totals equals NYPD-PD_RRP_T_TOT-A (2015 to 2021, the only years the OFR serves) on 364 of 365 weeks, the exception being the week of 2021-01-06; the securities-borrowed pair equals NYPD-PD_SB_T_TOT-A on 535 of 561 weeks, and the 26 weeks that differ all fall from 2022-01-05 to 2025-10-15, the New York Fed sum being larger (by about USD 4.5 to 5.3 billion in the first weeks of 2022). The differences are stated on the page and are not resolved here.

units: USD millions in the file; the level is read in USD billions (the sum of the four totals over 1,000)
as_of_week: each observation is dated by its as-of date, a Wednesday, and reports the position on that Wednesday (the New York Fed's 'previous week's statistics' on the Thursday it is released)

release.day_and_time: Thursdays at approximately 4:15 p.m. America/New_York, with the previous week's statistics

evidence.text: Data are updated on Thursdays at approximately 4:15 p.m. with the previous week's statistics.
evidence.snapshot: tests/fixtures/snapshots/nyfed-pd-financing/primary-dealers-statistics.html (sha256 and retrieval instant in manifest.json, keyid release-page); the test test_the_release_page_states_the_day_and_time_the_declaration_cites reads the sentence from the tracked bytes
evidence.agreement: the registry already dates the other FR 2004 series (nyfed_fr2004) as published on the Thursday of the following week, six business days after the Wednesday, from the same release schedule; the declared instant here is the same

release.declared_instant: 6 market business days after the as-of Wednesday, at 16:30 America/New_York: the Thursday of the following week, a holiday moving it to the next business day (metadata/market_holidays.json). 16:30 is the conservative instant within the release day against the page's 'approximately 4:15 p.m.', and it is the instant the registry declares for nyfed_fr2004
release.consequence: a decision at 16:00 on the release Thursday cannot read that week: the first decision that can is the next business day's. The release-day instant is tested (tests/test_s3c_pd.py, ReleaseDayTests)
release.not_established: the page says 'approximately' and no archive of past release times was read; the earlier of the two readings (4:15 p.m.) would not change any decision, since the decision instant is 16:00 and both fall after it

transform.level: the sum of the four totals, in USD billions; a week with any of the four withheld ('*', confidentiality) has no level: no observation, never 0
transform.state: the z-score of the latest public level against the weeks before it: (level - mean) / stdev (sample) over the defined levels of the 52 as-of weeks before the as-of week w* of that level; w* is the latest as-of week released at the decision instant that has a level
transform.undefined_when: no released week has a level; fewer than 13 of the 52 weeks before w* have one; or their standard deviation is not positive. The term is then 0, as an unknown scarcity state reads 0 in (s3)
transform.carry: the latest public level is carried over withheld weeks, however many (the directive's 'latest public level'); the number of weeks between the latest public week and w* is reported on the page for every decision day with a state, and no limit is set on it, a limit being a threshold nobody has set. The minimum of 13 is a quarter of the year, chosen from how many weeks are withheld in 2025 and 2026 (data availability, read before any score) and not from any score
transform.not_tuned: one transform, declared here; the alternatives named in the directive (a 13-week change) were not tried

limitations: The tracked snapshot is the latest revised vintage of each series as the New York Fed API served it on the retrieval date (manifest.json), not first prints. The series are not known to be revised often, but no first-print vintage was read, so a revision after the release is not excluded.

A figure the New York Fed withheld for confidentiality is '*'. In the tracked files 94 weeks of PDSIRRA-UTSETTOT, 13 of PDSIRRA-UTSTTOT and 69 of PDSIOSB-UTSTTOT are withheld (counted by the tests and the page from the files), so a week with a level is about two weeks in three since 2018 and about one in two in 2025 and 2026. The last three weeks of the tracked file are '*' for PDSIRRA-UTSETTOT; whether they are a withholding or a not-yet-filled value cannot be told from the file.
The Treasury rows are used, as the chart's mnemonics are (T). Other collateral classes (agency, MBS, corporate, equities) are not in the level.

proposed_registry_entry.limitation: One row per series per as-of date. A value of '*' is a figure the New York Fed withheld for confidentiality: it yields no observation, never 0.0. The snapshot is the latest revised vintage, not first prints.

release_lag.note: Six business days from a Wednesday as-of date is the Thursday of the following week (2026-08-26 becomes available 2026-09-03), at 16:30 America/New_York, the conservative instant within the release day against the page's 'approximately 4:15 p.m.'. Business days are counted on metadata/market_holidays.json. The same declaration as nyfed_fr2004's, from the same release schedule.
